headword: {士族階級|しぞくかいきゅう}
gloss: the samurai class; the shizoku class

definitions.gloss: the samurai class; the former-warrior (shizoku) class
definitions.explanation: The social class made up of former samurai families, an official category designated in the Meiji era after feudal warrior status was abolished.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{士族階級|しぞくかいきゅう}の{出身|しゅっしん}だ。
examples.english: He comes from the samurai class.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{士族階級|しぞくかいきゅう}の{特権|とっけん}は{失|うしな}われた。
examples.english: In the Meiji era, the privileges of the samurai class were lost.

examples.japanese: {士族階級|しぞくかいきゅう}の{多|おお}くは、{職|しょく}を{失|うしな}って{生活|せいかつ}に{苦|くる}しんだ。
examples.english: Many of the former samurai class lost their positions and struggled to make a living.

notes:
Composed of {士族|しぞく} ('former-samurai family class') + {階級|かいきゅう} ('class, rank'). {士族|しぞく} was an official social category created in the Meiji period for ex-samurai households.

ETYMOLOGY:
After the feudal system was dismantled, samurai lost their stipends and privileges. The phrase {士族|しぞく}の{商法|しょうほう} ('samurai's way of doing business') mocks their often-unsuccessful ventures into commerce.

RELATED WORDS:
- {華族|かぞく}: the peerage/nobility class of the same era
- {平民|へいみん}: commoners
